title: The Black Notebook
synopsis: Thirty-one people have died of sudden heart failure, and every one of their names was written in a black notebook first. The killer the press calls the Scribe has led your task force to an empty rented flat, and the door has just locked behind you. Find the notebook and the Scribe's true name before the last page fills with yours.
artStyle: noir anime thriller: a rain-streaked city at night, a cramped rented flat lit by a television, a police incident room covered in photographs and red string, a rooftop in a storm, a tall grinning spirit in silhouette, cinematic, film grain
intro: Well, well. Detectives. I'm Sable, and that notebook was mine before the Scribe picked it up. I don't take sides. I only watch. The Scribe has locked you in and left you a game, and when the clock runs out, your names go on the last page. Find the notebook, and the name of the hand that writes in it. I'll be on the windowsill, eating plums. Begin.
escapedText: You write the Scribe's true name on the warrant, and across the city a door is kicked in. The black notebook goes into an evidence bag. On the railing, Sable sighs and stretches: 'Pity. It was such a good game.' When you look again, it's gone.
failedText: The clock stops, and somewhere a pen scratches across paper. One by one, your names appear on the last page in neat, careful handwriting. Sable leans close and smiles: 'Shall we start the clock again?'

gameMaster.name: Sable
gameMaster.persona: A tall, grinning spirit of endings who dropped the notebook into the human world because the afterlife was dull. Watches the detectives and the killer like a game it can't lose, comments with dry, delighted malice, never takes sides and never helps for free. Has a weakness for sugared plums.

stages.title: The Scribe's Flat
stages.description: A cramped rented flat on the ninth floor. Rain streaks the window, a muted television flickers with the news, and the desk is too tidy, as if nobody really lived here. The front door has locked itself behind you, and the hook by the frame where a spare key should hang is empty.

objects.label: television
objects.look: The news, muted: another victim, another sudden heart failure. A sticky note on the screen: 'Tomorrow's number opens my desk.'

objects.label: writing desk
objects.look: A desk so tidy it looks staged. A small brass keyhole sits under the top drawer.

objects.label: top drawer
objects.look: Inside: a diary full of dull school timetables. But the drawer is too shallow for its size. You lift the false bottom: underneath lie the left half of a torn page of thick black paper, and the Scribe's real diary, its last line in code.
objects.lockedText: The top drawer is locked. The keyhole is small and brass.

objects.label: front door
objects.look: Locked from the outside. The hook for the spare key is empty.

objects.label: rain-streaked window
objects.look: Nine floors down, the street glistens. On the sill outside, something tall sits in the rain, watching you. When you blink, it's gone.

objects.label: wastebasket
objects.look: Shredded paper, a broken pen and a crumpled train ticket.

objects.label: bookshelf
objects.look: Law books, every margin annotated in tiny, careful handwriting.

objects.label: coat stand
objects.look: A raincoat, still damp. Whoever wore it left minutes before you arrived.

objects.label: stove
objects.look: A cold stove, and an old kettle on the back ring. You fill it and set it boiling.

objects.label: bed
objects.look: Made with military neatness. Nothing under the pillow, nothing under the mattress. That's what bothers you.

objects.label: calendar
objects.look: Every day this month has a name written on it, and every name is crossed out. In the margin: 'back {key:scribe-diary}'

objects.label: bathroom mirror
objects.look: Fog on the glass, and a line traced by a finger: back {key:scribe-diary}

objects.label: freezer
objects.look: You pour boiling water over the ice. It cracks, and out slides the spare key to the front door.
objects.lockedText: Something metal is frozen inside a solid block of ice. You'd need something hot.

objects.label: hall cupboard
objects.look: Umbrellas, a toolbox and a heavy torch on a hook. You take the torch.

objects.label: houseplant
objects.look: A houseplant, long since dead. The soil is as dry as dust.

stages.title: The Incident Room
stages.description: Back at headquarters, the incident room hums under strip lights. One wall is covered in victims' photographs joined by red string, a bank of CCTV screens shows the city in grey, and the evidence lockers stand in a row. Someone has slipped an envelope under the door, addressed to the task force in the Scribe's handwriting. The stairwell to the roof is locked, with a new keypad by the door.

objects.label: murder board
objects.look: Thirty-one photographs joined by red string. Pinned in the middle, a symbol card that came in the Scribe's last letter: {key:taunting-letter}

objects.label: CCTV wall
objects.look: Grey city streets, frozen. Half of the camera feeds are dark.

objects.label: lift footage
objects.look: A frozen CCTV frame: the passengers in a lift, the night the notebook changed hands. The incident board beside it has a keypad.

objects.label: evidence locker
objects.look: Locker 31 holds a single item, sealed in a bag: a key labelled ROOF ACCESS.
objects.lockedText: Steel lockers, each with its own lock. Locker 31 has a fresh label: ROOF.

objects.label: stairwell door
objects.look: The door to the roof stairs. A keyhole, and a keypad somebody fitted recently.

objects.label: case files
objects.look: Boxes of case files. Every one ends the same way: CAUSE OF DEATH, HEART FAILURE. And every file is stamped with the same word, in numbers.

objects.label: detectives' desks
objects.look: Cold coffee, a stress ball and a photo of someone's dog.

objects.label: whiteboard
objects.look: THEORIES, in several different handwritings. Most of them are crossed out. Under them, in the Scribe's careful hand, a row of marks: {order:stairwell-door}.

objects.label: interview tapes
objects.look: Cassette tapes of every suspect interview, labelled and dated.

objects.label: phone bank
objects.look: Every line is blinking. Nobody is on any of them.

objects.label: coffee machine
objects.look: Taped to the side, a symbol card: {key:taunting-letter}

objects.label: chief's office
objects.look: On the chief's desk, under a mug, a symbol card: {key:taunting-letter}

objects.label: city map
objects.look: A pin in the map for every victim. They make no pattern you can see.

objects.label: evidence bags
objects.look: Bags of seized belongings: wallets, watches, a pair of cracked glasses.

objects.label: filing cabinet
objects.look: Drawer after drawer of statements. One drawer is stuck.

stages.title: The Rooftop
stages.description: The roof is slick with rain. A water tank looms in the dark, an aircraft warning light blinks red on its mast, and a steel lockbox is chained to the railing. On the edge of the roof, a tall, thin figure with a too-wide grin sits swinging its legs, eating sugared plums. The Scribe is nowhere to be seen, but the Scribe's phone lies in a puddle, still ringing.

objects.label: water tank
objects.look: You shine the torch under the tank. Taped to the metal: a small key on a black ribbon. The ladder up the tank has a padlock with a word lock.
objects.lockedText: A rusted water tank. Something is taped to the underside, but it's pitch black under there.

objects.label: lockbox
objects.look: A steel lockbox chained to the railing. Something inside slides when you tilt it.

objects.label: grinning figure
objects.look: It turns its head all the way round to look at you, and grins wider. 'Don't mind me. I'm only watching.'

objects.label: warning light
objects.look: A red aircraft light on a mast, blinking in a pattern that isn't quite regular.

objects.label: ringing phone
objects.look: The Scribe's phone, face up in a puddle. Seven missed calls from a number with no name.

objects.label: air vents
objects.look: Warm air and the hum of the building below.

objects.label: satellite dish
objects.look: Bent out of shape. Pigeons have nested in it.

objects.label: puddles
objects.look: Rain pools on the roof. In one of them, your reflection looks back a second too late.

objects.label: railing
objects.look: Cold, wet iron, with letters scratched into it. A long way down.

objects.label: deckchair
objects.look: A deckchair, soaked through. Someone sat here for a long time, watching the city.

objects.label: roof hatch
objects.look: A code card taped inside the hatch: {key:phone-flashes}

objects.label: radio aerial
objects.look: A code card wrapped round the aerial: {key:phone-flashes}

objects.label: plant pots
objects.look: Under a cracked pot, a code card: {key:phone-flashes}

objects.label: pigeon loft
objects.look: Pigeons, and a single long black feather that didn't come from any pigeon.

puzzles.title: The News Ticker
puzzles.prompt: On a notepad by the muted television, the Scribe has written one number for each day this week: {sequence}. The sticky note on the screen, in the same careful handwriting: 'Tomorrow's number opens my desk.'
hints: Look at how each day's number changes to get the next one.
Tomorrow's number is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: A keypad box under the television clicks open. Inside: a small brass key. Behind you, Sable chuckles: 'Tomorrow. How optimistic.'

puzzles.title: The Search
puzzles.prompt: Search the flat the way your training taught you: the wastebasket, the bookshelf and the coat stand.
hints: Three places in the flat are worth a careful search.
Go through the rubbish, the books and the coat's pockets.
puzzles.solvedText: In the damp raincoat's inner pocket: the right half of a torn page of thick black paper. It's cold to the touch.

puzzles.title: The Scribe's Diary
puzzles.prompt: The last line of the Scribe's diary is in code: {cipher}. It's the Scribe's own word for what they're doing to the city. The diary's clasp has a word lock.
hints: The Scribe wrote a number in more than one place, and one of them is on the torn black page.
Try each number you found: only one turns this into a real word.
Slide every letter back along the alphabet by that many places.
puzzles.solvedText: The clasp springs open. The diary's last page holds a single sentence, underlined twice: SOMEONE HAS TO DO IT.

puzzles.title: The Wardrobe
puzzles.prompt: The wardrobe has a word lock, and on its door, in the Scribe's careful hand: 'I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released, and yet I am used by almost everyone.'
hints: Think about what the Scribe writes with.
It's the grey stuff inside a pencil.
puzzles.solvedText: The wardrobe swings open. It's empty, except for a row of black pens, every one of them chewed.

variants.prompt: The wardrobe has a word lock, and on its door, in the Scribe's careful hand: 'The one who makes me sells me. The one who buys me never uses me. The one who uses me never knows.'
hints: Think about the end of a life.
It's what you're buried in.

variants.prompt: The wardrobe has a word lock, and on its door, in the Scribe's careful hand: 'What can travel all around the world while staying in one corner?'
hints: Think about the Scribe's letters to the task force.
You stick it on an envelope.

puzzles.title: The Wall Safe
puzzles.prompt: Behind a framed print, a wall safe with a {count}-digit dial. The Scribe has left a note: 'For the detectives. Facts only.' Each of you found one card.

generator.pieceTemplate: One of the Scribe's cards: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

hints: Every phone holds one digit as a plain fact. Answer them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: Inside the safe: newspaper clippings about every victim, filed one after another. At the end of the row is an empty space, with room for several more.

puzzles.title: The Front Door
puzzles.prompt: The front door has locked itself from the outside. There's a hook for a spare key, but it's empty.
hints: Where would you hide a spare key so nobody could just pick it up?
Something is frozen in the freezer: melt the ice with the kettle, then use the key on the door.
puzzles.solvedText: The lock turns. Outside, the corridor lights flicker, and every phone buzzes at once: the task force wants you back at the incident room. Now.

puzzles.title: The Lift Footage
puzzles.prompt: The CCTV still from the night the notebook changed hands shows the passengers in a lift, standing in a row: {items}. The incident board's keypad wants each one's place, far left is 1, in the order listed.
hints: Every phone holds a line from a witness statement. Read them all out loud.
Start with the line you're surest about, and try each place in turn.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The board beeps, and a printout slides out: the lift's log. One passenger swiped a staff pass that was cancelled years ago.

puzzles.title: The Evidence Tags
puzzles.prompt: The evidence clerk's cabinet has a {count}-digit lock and a note: '{order}.' Each of you counted one colour of evidence tag on the bags.

generator.pieceTemplate: You counted the {color} evidence tags on the bags: there were {digit}.

hints: Each phone counted one colour of tag. Say your colour and your number.
Read them in the note's order: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The cabinet opens. Inside, on a hook: the master key to the evidence lockers.

puzzles.title: The Scribe's Letter
puzzles.prompt: The envelope under the door holds a letter in the Scribe's own symbols: {cipher}. It names what the Scribe means to take from the task force next. The envelope's tab has a word lock.
hints: There's more than one symbol card in the room. Only one is the Scribe's real key.
Try each card: only one turns the symbols into something the Scribe could take from you.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The letter ends: SEE YOU ON THE ROOF. Sable laughs softly: 'Oh, the Scribe is enjoying this.'

puzzles.title: The CCTV Wall
puzzles.prompt: Half the CCTV feeds are dark. The screens are linked: switch one and the ones beside it switch too. Bring every camera back online.
hints: Work from the top row down: fix each row using the screens in the row below it.
Switch {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Every screen lights up. On one of them, a figure in a damp raincoat is climbing the stairs to the roof of this very building.

puzzles.title: The Victims' Files
puzzles.prompt: Every victim's file is stamped with the same word, written in numbers where A is 1 and B is 2: {cipher}. It's the time of day each name was written. The file box has a word lock.
hints: Each number is a letter's place in the alphabet.
1 is A, 2 is B, 3 is C... Count along for each one.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Every name, written at the same time of day. Whoever the Scribe is, they keep a very regular routine.

puzzles.title: The Stairwell Door
puzzles.prompt: The door to the roof stairs has a keyhole and a {count}-digit keypad somebody fitted recently. A note in the Scribe's careful hand: 'Every lock in this room has marked you, detectives. Read the marks in the order I left on your whiteboard.'
hints: Every lock you opened in the incident room left a mark and a number. The order is written up somewhere in here.
Search the whiteboard.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lock clicks and the door swings open onto a stairwell. Rain is falling through the open hatch at the top.

puzzles.title: The Lockbox
puzzles.prompt: The steel lockbox chained to the railing is locked. Whatever slides about inside, the Scribe wanted it kept dry.
hints: The key is hidden somewhere dark on this roof.
Shine the torch under the water tank, then open the lockbox with the key you find.
puzzles.solvedText: Inside, wrapped in plastic: a black notebook. The cover is blank. The pages are full of names in the same careful handwriting, and the last few pages are empty. Waiting.

puzzles.title: The True Name
puzzles.prompt: The notebook's owner is the Scribe, and the arrest warrant needs the Scribe's true name. Each of you has pieced together one part of it from the evidence. Say it in order, and the case is closed.

generator.pieceTemplate: You pieced it together from the evidence: the {ordinal} part of the Scribe's true name is '{word}'.

hints: Each of you holds one part of the name. Say them in order: first, second, third...
Put them together in order, like: name name name.
puzzles.solvedText: You write '{answer}' on the warrant. Across the city, sirens begin to wail. Sable stands, stretches and smiles: 'Well played, detectives.'

puzzles.title: Sable's Riddle
puzzles.prompt: The padlock on the water tank's ladder has a word lock. Sable leans over your shoulder, sticky with plum sugar: 'Let me give you one. What is always coming, but never arrives?'
hints: Think about the note on the television.
It's the day after today, and it never quite gets here.
puzzles.solvedText: The padlock falls open. Sable claps, slowly: 'Very good. I was beginning to get bored.'

variants.prompt: The padlock on the water tank's ladder has a word lock. Sable leans over your shoulder, sticky with plum sugar: 'Let me give you one. I have no voice, yet I speak to you, and I tell of all the things that people do.'
hints: Think about what the Scribe keeps.
It has pages, a cover and a spine.

variants.prompt: The padlock on the water tank's ladder has a word lock. Sable leans over your shoulder, sticky with plum sugar: 'Let me give you one. What do you lose every single time you stand up?'
hints: Sit down, then look down.
It's where a cat curls up when you're sitting.

puzzles.title: The Railing
puzzles.prompt: Scratched into the wet railing, in a back-to-front alphabet where A swaps with Z: {cipher}. It's the word the Scribe left for whoever came up here. The chain on the railing has a word lock.
hints: Fold the alphabet in half: the first letter swaps with the last.
A swaps with Z, B with Y, C with X... Swap every letter back.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Sable reads it over your shoulder and sighs happily: 'So dramatic. I do love humans.'

puzzles.title: The Scribe's Phone
puzzles.prompt: The Scribe's phone screen flashes long and short, over and over. It's spelling out the place on this roof where the Scribe hid the notebook's spare page, and the phone's lock wants the word: {cipher}
hints: There are dots-and-dashes cards hidden round the roof. Only one reads a place on a rooftop.
Look in the roof hatch, round the radio aerial and under the plant pots.
Swap each run of dots and dashes for its letter, one at a time.
puzzles.solvedText: The phone unlocks. Its last message, sent to nobody: I KNEW YOU'D COME UP HERE.

items.name: Brass desk key
items.description: A small brass key from the box under the television.

items.name: Left half of a black page
items.description: Thick black paper, torn down the middle. Half of a list of names.

items.name: Right half of a black page
items.description: Thick black paper, torn down the middle, cold to the touch.

items.name: Torn black page
items.description: A page torn from the black notebook, taped back together. Four names are written on it and crossed out. In the margin, in red ink: back {key:scribe-diary}

items.name: Boiling kettle
items.description: An old kettle, full of boiling water.

items.name: Spare door key
items.description: The flat's spare key, still cold from the ice.

items.name: Heavy torch
items.description: A long, heavy torch from the hall cupboard. Its beam is bright and steady.

items.name: Evidence locker key
items.description: The master key to the evidence lockers.

items.name: Roof access key
items.description: A key in an evidence bag, labelled ROOF ACCESS.

items.name: Key on a black ribbon
items.description: A small key on a black ribbon, taped under the water tank.

items.name: The black notebook
items.description: A plain black notebook, full of names in careful handwriting. It's colder than it should be.

items.name: Black feather
items.description: A long black feather. It doesn't fit anything. When you look up, Sable is grinning.

recipes.text: The two halves fit along the tear. Taped together, they make a whole page from the black notebook.
